'''Ray Alden Kunze''' (March 7, 1928 – May 21, 2014) was an American mathematician who chaired the mathematics departments at the [[University of California, Irvine]] and the [[University of Georgia]].<ref name="obit">{{citation|title=Ray Alden Kunze|department=Paid Obituaries|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=July 12, 2014|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/latimes/obituary.aspx?pid=171699262}}</ref><ref name="ded"/> His mathematical research concerned the [[representation theory]] of [[group (mathematics)|groups]] and [[noncommutative harmonic analysis]].<ref name="ded"/>

Kunze was born in [[Des Moines, Iowa]] and grew up near [[Milwaukee, Wisconsin]].<ref name="obit"/><ref name="ded">[https://www.ams.org/books/conm/191/conm191-endmatter.pdf Dedication to ''Representation theory and harmonic analysis''], pp. ix–x.</ref> He began his undergraduate studies at [[Denison University]] but transferred to the [[University of Chicago]] after two years, and earned bachelor's and master's degrees in mathematics.<ref name="ded"/> After working as a military mathematical analyst,<ref name="obit"/><ref name="ded"/> he returned to the University of Chicago, and earned his Ph.D. in 1957 with a dissertation on [[Fourier transformation]]s supervised by [[Irving Segal]].<ref name="ded"/><ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|id=6466}}.</ref> As well as his positions at UCI and Georgia, he also worked at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], [[Brandeis University]], and [[Washington University in St. Louis]].<ref name="obit"/><ref name="ded"/> He has over 50 [[academic genealogy|academic descendants]], many of them through his students [[Paul Sally]] at Brandeis and Edward N. Wilson at Washington University.<ref name="mg"/>

With his advisor [[Irving Segal]], Kunze was the author of the textbook ''Integrals and Operators'' (McGraw-Hill, 1968; 2nd ed., Grundlehren der Mathematischen Wissenschaften 228, Springer, 1978).<ref>Reviews of ''Integrals and Operators'' by S. K. Berberian, 1st ed., {{MR|0217244}}, and 2nd ed., {{MR|0486380}}.</ref> With Kenneth M. Hoffman he was the author of ''Linear Algebra'' (Prentice-Hall, 1961; 2nd ed., Pearson, 1971).<ref name="ded"/><ref>Review of ''Linear algebra'' by [[Leon Mirsky]], {{MR|0125849}}; for the 2nd ed., see {{MR|0276251}}.</ref>

In 1994, a special session on [[representation theory]] and [[harmonic analysis]] was held in honor of Kunze as part of the  889th meeting of the American Mathematical Society, and the papers from the session were published as a [[festschrift]].<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Ton-That | first1 = Tuong
 | last2 = Gross | first2 = Kenneth I.
 | last3 = Richards | first3 = Donald St. P.
 | last4 = Sally | first4 = Paul J. Jr.
 | doi = 10.1090/conm/191
 | isbn = 0-8218-0310-7
 | mr = 1365528
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI
 | series = Contemporary Mathematics
 | title = Representation theory and harmonic analysis: Papers from the conference held in honor of Ray A. Kunze at the AMS Special Session, Cincinnati, Ohio, January 12–14, 1994
 | volume = 191
 | year = 1995}}.</ref>
In 2012, Kunze was recognized as one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2015-01-26.</ref>
